generatedFrom.counts: a straddle is an event in time — the shutter open across a pattern change — not a decoded error. Nothing here renders or decodes a frame, so what a straddled photograph costs a calibration is unmeasured and needs its own experiment.
generatedFrom.driftModel: a fixed per-capture rate error, not a random walk: two crystals at steady temperature differ by a roughly constant rate over the twenty minutes a capture takes. The ppm band is engineering-typical and has not been measured against a camera beside a sphere.

verdict.statement: Where the first shutter lands in the dwell decides an untethered capture, and it decides it far more than the crystal does. At the emitter's default 2 s dwell and a 1/4 s exposure, with the loosest crystal in the sweep (100 ppm): an operator who starts the camera at no particular phase ruined 728 of 2000 captures (36.4%), and 589 of them lost a whole camera position, every frame of it, from that position's first photograph to its last. That rate is not a property of the clocks: a shot opening at phase p straddles when p > dwell - exposure, so a start at no particular phase straddles its first frame with probability exposure / dwell, 12.5% here, and drift is far too small to move it afterwards. A capture is 3 positions and the emitter stops between them, so that gamble is taken 3 times over and the capture-level risk is 33.0%. Shooting on the page's own tick instead puts the shutter a reaction time after the boundary — the roomiest place in the dwell — and ruined 13 (0.7%); deliberately aiming mid-dwell ruined 0 (0.0%). Clock drift really is negligible at this dwell — 27 ms accumulated across the 136 frames of one camera position, against margins of 750 ms above a mid-dwell shot and 1000 ms below — so what a tether removes is not drift but the start-phase gamble. A hand-pressed remote is worse and differently shaped: at a uniform start it touched 1981 of 2000 (99.0%) and on the tick still 2000 (100.0%), with scattered straddles rather than one continuous ruined stretch — only 0 of those lost a whole position end to end.
